scope: Selected sources informing an explicitly artificial circular-phase sensitivity analysis, not astrological outcome prediction or calibration.

sources.title: American Statistical Association, official release about its 2016 p-value statement
supports: P-values do not quantify the probability a studied hypothesis is true.
Full reporting and effect size matter; thresholds alone do not support scientific/business decisions.
sources.limitations: This is the official press release/summary, not the full journal article.
sources.rights: Only bibliographic metadata and original methodological paraphrase redistributed. Source documents remain outside Git; the official R source is GPL-2-or-later.

sources.title: Phipson and Smyth, Permutation P-values Should Never Be Zero
sources.locator: Author PDF published 31 October 2010, corrected 9 February 2011; abstract and sections 4–6
supports: Identity/plus-one convention avoids spuriously zero sampled-randomization values.
Sampling with and without replacement have distinct derivations and assumptions.
sources.limitations: Its valid-randomization premises are not a claim that deterministic calendar series generate valid real-world outcome p-values.
sources.rights: Only bibliographic metadata and original methodological paraphrase redistributed. Source documents remain outside Git; the official R source is GPL-2-or-later.

sources.title: Schreiber and Schmitz, Surrogate time series
supports: Surrogate methods require an explicit null and careful interpretation.
Post-selection, periodic endpoint mismatch and nonstationarity can invalidate naive interpretations.
sources.limitations: The project circular-phase comparison is original; it does not reproduce the paper’s Fourier-surrogate algorithms. The downloaded PDF prints a 2024 typesetting date alongside 1999 arXiv metadata; hash identifies the actual inspected bytes.
sources.rights: Only bibliographic metadata and original methodological paraphrase redistributed. Source documents remain outside Git; the official R source is GPL-2-or-later.

sources.title: R stats official p.adjust documentation
sources.locator: Details: Holm; larger family n; source references
supports: Holm adjustment uses the full family size.
Strong family-wise control requires suitable raw p-values; arbitrary-dependence allowance does not validate a misspecified null.
sources.limitations: The original Holm (1979) JSTOR body was not accessible; reading the original paper is not claimed.
sources.rights: Only bibliographic metadata and original methodological paraphrase redistributed. Source documents remain outside Git; the official R source is GPL-2-or-later.

sources.title: R stats official p.adjust.R implementation
sources.locator: holm branch: ordered scaled values, running maximum, original ordering
supports: Independent implementation-level confirmation of the Holm formula used here.
sources.limitations: The retrieved trunk source is mutable upstream; the downloaded SHA identifies the inspected version. No R runtime is required by the web application.
sources.rights: Only bibliographic metadata and original methodological paraphrase redistributed. Source documents remain outside Git; the official R source is GPL-2-or-later.

sources.title: SciPy permutation_test official documentation
sources.locator: alternative, exact/randomizedreference, plus-one convention and inclusive tails
supports: Includes equality in one-sided null tails and explains identity correction.
Reports null/statistic convention; two-sided definitions are not universal.
sources.limitations: The project uses absolute Spearman tails, not SciPy’s doubled-minimum convention; SciPy is not a browser dependency.
